title: Australian Tax Rates 2024-25
content: Australian resident tax rates for 2024-25: $0-$18,200 = 0%, $18,201-$45,000 = 16c per $1 over $18,200, $45,001-$135,000 = $4,288 plus 30c per $1 over $45,000, $135,001-$190,000 = $31,288 plus 37c per $1 over $135,000, $190,001+ = $51,638 plus 45c per $1 over $190,000. These rates exclude the 2% Medicare levy.

title: Medicare Levy 2024-25
content: Medicare levy is 2% of your taxable income for most Australian residents. You may not need to pay if your income is below $27,222 (2024-25). Higher income earners without private health insurance may also pay Medicare levy surcharge (MLS) of 1-1.5% depending on income level.

title: Medicare Levy 2025-26
content: Medicare levy is 2% of your taxable income for most Australian residents. You may not need to pay if your income is below $27,222 (2025-26). Higher income earners without private health insurance may also pay Medicare levy surcharge (MLS) of 1-1.5% depending on income level.

title: Working From Home Tax Deductions 2024-25
content: You can claim 70 cents per hour worked from home using the fixed rate method for 2024-25. Keep records of hours worked and have receipts for additional expenses. This covers electricity, gas, phone, internet, stationery, and computer consumables. You cannot claim separate phone/internet expenses when using this method.

title: Working From Home Tax Deductions 2025-26
content: You can claim 70 cents per hour worked from home using the fixed rate method for 2025-26. Keep records of hours worked and have receipts for additional expenses. This covers electricity, gas, phone, internet, stationery, and computer consumables. You cannot claim separate phone/internet expenses when using this method.

title: Work-Related Car Expenses 2024-25
content: Car expenses can be claimed using two methods: 1) Cents per kilometre - 88 cents per km up to 5,000km maximum, covers all car expenses. 2) Logbook method - claim actual expenses based on work-use percentage. Requires 12-week logbook and receipts. Cannot claim normal home-to-work commuting. Only travel between jobs, client visits, or work-related destinations qualify.

title: How Progressive Tax System Works
content: Australia uses a progressive tax system where higher income is taxed at higher rates. You only pay the higher rate on income above each bracket threshold, not on your entire income. For example, if you earn $50,000, you pay 0% on first $18,200, then 16% on the remaining $31,800 up to $45,000, then 30% on the final $5,000.
